composition_parti.rule: additive-vernacular: openings are placed by use and by the corner-clearance rule (window_grouping_rule, below), not composed to a bilateral axis; the apparent front symmetry of a double pen is an artefact of two identical pens, not a compositional decision.
composition_parti.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'strict-bilateral-odd-bay' from english-georgian, directly contradicted by the node's own proportional_system.symmetry field, which reads 'additive-vernacular' verbatim.

roof_form.rule: A simple gable roof over each pen, front- or side-facing depending on the combination; no hip, no complex form -- own defining_characteristics: 'Riven shingle or shake roof on light pole rafters or purlins, with no ridge beam required.'
roof_form.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'front-gable' from germanic-vernacular as an absolute rule ('the gable, not the eave, is the composed and entered face'), overstating a Continental compositional claim this frontier vernacular's own text does not make -- pen orientation is a plan decision (see dogtrot-vernacular and appalachian-log-house), not a facade composition rule.

roof_pitch.rule: Roof pitch 8:12 to 12:12 for riven shingles; lower pitches fail with hand-split roofing (own hard constraint, and own typical_ratios).
roof_pitch.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Nordic pitch pair expressed in DEGREES (18-30 deg) rather than this schema's rise_in_12 unit used everywhere else in the corpus, and keyed to a snow-load/rain-shedding split with no demonstrated relevance to this style's own Appalachian/Ozark/Piedmont climate range.

roof_material.rule: Riven shingle or shake roof on light pole rafters or purlins, with no ridge beam required (own defining_characteristics #6).

projection_in.note: Own hard constraint c04: at least 18 in, 24-36 preferred.

eave_condition.rule: Eave overhang at least 18 in (24-36 preferred) on all elevations to keep water off the chinking; boxed soffits and clipped eaves destroy the wall (own hard constraint c04, soft).
eave_condition.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Mediterranean paired-bracket/corbelled-tile eave rule (mediterranean-vernacular) whose own two source members' overhang figures 'barely overlap' by that node's own admission -- no relationship to a log wall's chinking-protection logic. Specified (not extended) so the wrong Mediterranean base is replaced outright rather than merged onto.

rake_condition.rule: The rake carries the same eave overhang as the eave itself (eave_condition, above) -- at least 18 in, 24-36 preferred -- for the same chinking-protection reason, not a separately-derived Fachwerk verge figure.
rake_condition.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a German Fachwerk verge-overhang rule stated in millimetres against a rain-off-the-daub logic (protecting an infill panel this construction does not have).

gable_treatment.rule: The gable is the log wall carried up in diminishing courses to the ridge, or a light-frame infill above the plate -- never a half-timbered composed face in the German Fachwerk sense.
gable_treatment.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'half-timbered, jettied and jointed at the German street front' from germanic-vernacular -- the Continental Fachwerk vocabulary this node's own distinguished_from entry against german-pennsylvania-colonial explicitly separates itself from.

chimney.rule: Chimney at the gable end, exterior or partly exterior, of stone, or of stick-and-clay in the poorest work (own defining_characteristics #7).
chimney.note: CASCADE FIX -- one of the most consequential in this file. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'central-single-stack' from german-pennsylvania-colonial, whose own hard constraint c01 states 'moving it to the gable ends dissolves the plan type' -- the exact opposite of this node's own defining characteristic. This node's own distinguished_from entry against german-pennsylvania-colonial is explicit that the Continental central-chimney Flurkuchenhaus plan is a DIFFERENT node from this one: 'Where the plan is Anglo... the building belongs here.'

height_proportion.rule: Wall height 8-10 log courses, roughly 7-9 ft to the plate per storey (own typical_ratios); no jettied oversailing storey, which presupposes a framed floor structure a solid log wall does not build.
height_proportion.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a German Fachwerk jetty rule (each storey oversails the one below by 200-400 mm on projecting floor-beam ends) -- a half-timbered framing device with no equivalent in a solid-log wall, which has no floor beams to project.

construction_type.rule_append: Corner joints are notched (V, half-dovetail, full dovetail, square or saddle) and, except in saddle notching, slope outward to shed water (own hard constraint c02); log faces are hewn flat on interior and exterior, wall thickness 6-9 in after hewing (own hard constraint c03).
construction_type.note: Restates own c02/c03 directly on top of the correctly-inherited 'construction=log' base fact from nordic-alpine-vernacular.

wall_thickness_masonry.rule: There is no masonry wall in this construction; wall thickness is entirely a function of the hewn log (construction_type, already specified).
wall_thickness_masonry.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 400-700 mm Mediterranean load-bearing masonry thickness range with no relevance to a log wall.

water_table.rule: No water table; the wall is one continuous log assembly from sill to plate.

belt_course.rule: No belt course; nothing interrupts the log coursing.

corner_quoin.rule_append: The notch profile is regional: half-dovetail and full dovetail dominate the Upland South, square notching the Ozarks, V-notch Pennsylvania -- see the regional variant nodes for the specific figure.

cornice.rule: No classical cornice or entablature; the eave is the plate log and the roof structure directly, per own eave_condition.
cornice.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Georgian 'modillion-cornice' -- a classical entablature member directly contradicted by the family-level classical-apparatus prohibitions already correctly resolving below.

parapet.rule: No parapet; the roof is shown.
parapet.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Baroque 'balustraded' parapet -- both the classical device and the already-forbidden turned balustrade own classical-apparatus group correctly rules out elsewhere.

color_strategy.rule: Bare, weathered, unpainted log with a lime-white chinking band between courses; no Scandinavian falu-red tradition exists in the American channel.
color_strategy.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Nordic 'bare-weathered-unpainted, falu-red-white-trim' pairing; falu-red is a specifically Swedish paint tradition with no American log attestation anywhere in this node's own text, which instead describes 'the chinking is the maintenance problem and the visual signature both: a two-inch band of white lime between dark logs.'

window_type.rule: A small wood-framed opening cut into the log wall after the wall was raised, glazed with a single sash or, in the earliest work, an unglazed shuttered opening -- not a counterweighted double-hung sash box, which presupposes a wall thin enough to house it.
window_type.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Georgian counterweighted double-hung sash box from english-georgian, a wall-thickness and joinery system with no relationship to a solid 6-9 in hewn log wall.

window_proportion.rule: No fixed proportion; the opening is small and sized to interrupt as few log courses as possible, not composed to a ratio.
window_proportion.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Tudor wide-multi-light-grid proportion; window_grouping_rule (already correctly resolving from nordic-alpine-vernacular) already states directly that 'a large or ribboned opening is structurally impossible in a solid log wall' -- this restates the same fact for the proportion slot specifically.

window_head_masonry.rule: There is no masonry window head; construction_type (already specified) is solid log throughout, so window_head_wood is the only applicable slot.
window_head_masonry.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Renaissance 'semicircular-arch-impost-sprung' masonry head, structurally impossible in a log wall.

window_head_wood.rule: The head is a solid log spanning the opening directly, or a pegged wood lintel jamb -- no applied head assembly of any kind.
window_head_wood.note: Grounded in own hard constraint c05: 'their jambs must be pegged or spiked to the cut log ends.'

special_window.rule: No special window of any kind -- Venetian, Diocletian, or otherwise; own hard constraint c05: 'Corner windows and full-height glazed walls are structurally impossible in this system.'
special_window.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Palladian 'venetian-serliana' special window, a classical composite opening with zero structural relationship to a solid log wall.

entry_door.rule: There is no separate entry_door slot content beyond door_surround (already specified): a plain plank door hung in a pegged log frame. The wagon-scaled Grootdor is a North German barn-house device with no place in a domestic pen.
entry_door.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'grootdor-wagon-door' from north-german-hall-house -- a door sized to drive a loaded hay wagon through, absurd at the scale of a 16-20 ft domestic pen.

door_surround.rule: A plain wood door with pegged jambs against the cut log ends; no applied hood, moulding, or surround of any kind.
door_surround.note: Restates own hard constraint c05 more precisely than the inherited 'plain-hood' answer, which still implies an applied hood member this node's own construction logic does not support.

variants.note: A small detached log or frame outbuilding sited informally, consistent with the type's own additive, use-driven siting logic.
An attached bay would require a log span this system's own 16-20 ft wall limit (c01) cannot honestly accommodate without breaking the pen logic.

garage_strategy.rule: The car is housed in a small detached outbuilding, sited informally like any other frontier outbuilding -- never integrated into the pen itself.
garage_strategy.note: No historical precedent exists for this slot. Authored per docs/inheritance.md's guidance; this node's own status field reads 'living' and its own revival note describes an active modern kit-log industry, both of which support specifying rather than leaving this open.

porch_type.rule: Where a porch occurs at all it is a shallow shed roof extension on log or pole posts along the entry wall, never a temple-front portico.
porch_type.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Palladian 'pedimented-temple-front-portico' -- the single most incongruous leak found in this batch, a temple-front colonnade projected onto an 18x20 ft hewn-log pen.

porch_support.rule: Plain log or pole posts, unhewn or lightly hewn, never a classical column.
porch_support.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'ionic-or-corinthian-portico-columns, four or six across' from palladian.

steps_and_stoop.rule: A single stone slab or a short run of log or stone steps at grade -- not an external flight to a raised piano nobile.
steps_and_stoop.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Palladian external stair to a piano nobile raised 47 in above grade on a rusticated service basement -- this type has no raised principal floor or basement of that kind.

entry_sequence.rule: Direct: the door opens straight into the pen at grade, with no intervening stair, landing, or working ground floor to pass through.
entry_sequence.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Tuscan farmhouse rule about an external stair bypassing a ground-floor stalla (animal barn) -- a two-storey Mediterranean farmhouse section this one-storey pen does not have.

trim_family.rule: There is no applied interior trim family; the hewn log wall is its own finished surface. Where later frame additions occur they carry their own separate, un-derived trim.
trim_family.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Georgian 'gibbsian-bolection' classical trim family graded room by room -- own proportional_system.governing_logic states plainly 'there is no applied proportional system, and adding one falsifies the type.'

newel_balustrade.rule: No newel or balustrade; the stair is a ladder or an open boxed run with a plain rail if any (stair_position, already specified).
newel_balustrade.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Jacobean 'square-newel-obelisk-or-beast-finial' stair post -- a carved heraldic newel with no relationship to a ladder or boxed corner stair.

fireplace_surround.rule: A plain stone or clay-and-stick firebox opening, unornamented -- not an architectural chimneypiece of any kind.
fireplace_surround.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Jacobean 'two-storey marble-and-alabaster chimneypiece with caryatids and strapwork... often the single most expensive object in the house' -- about as far as this corpus's cascade travels from a frontier log cabin's own firebox.

floor_material.rule: Riven puncheon or sawn board floor, laid directly on sleepers -- no finish material.
floor_material.note: Grounded in appalachian-log-house's own long description: 'floored in riven puncheon or sawn boards.'

hardware.rule: Hand-forged iron strap hinges and a wood or iron thumb latch; no graded brass hardware.

variants.note: Two equal pens, two front doors, two end chimneys -- own massing_affinities.

The Continental German plan. Own distinguished_from entry against german-pennsylvania-colonial: 'Where the plan is Anglo -- hall, hall-and-parlor, double pen with two front doors -- the building belongs here.'

circulation_parti.rule: The plan is Anglo -- hall, hall-and-parlor, double pen with two front doors -- built up by pen combination, not the Continental three-room Flurkuchenhaus plan organized around a central chimney.
circulation_parti.note: CASCADE FIX -- directly grounded in the node's own distinguished_from entry, which the pre-fix cascade's german-pennsylvania-colonial binding contradicted outright.

hearth_position.rule: At the gable end of each pen (per chimney, above); a central stack shared between rooms is the Continental Flurkuchenhaus plan this node's own text distinguishes itself from.

stair_position.rule: A ladder or a boxed corner stair rising in the corner of the pen to the loft -- not a formal passage stair.
stair_position.note: Grounded in own long description: 'the loft above them is reached by a ladder or a boxed corner stair.'

room_adjacency_overrides.rule: Each pen is one undivided room; adjacency, where more than one pen exists, is pen-to-pen (directly, or across a dogtrot passage), never a livestock-and-family shared-floor arrangement.
room_adjacency_overrides.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a North German hall-house rule with livestock stalls and family sleeping cupboards sharing one undivided floor (the Diele/Kubbungen/Flett arrangement) -- a Continental barn-house plan with no relationship to the Anglo pen-and-loft plan already fixed at circulation_parti.

rules.statement: Each pen is one undivided room, and adjacency where more than one pen exists is pen-to-pen -- directly, or across a dogtrot passage -- never a livestock-and-family shared floor.
rules.why: Two claims of one kind: what a pen contains, and what may adjoin what. The second half is a prohibition the universal records do not make because they have no vocabulary for livestock in the house.

service_zone_strategy.rule: There is no separate service zone; the single pen is the whole house, and any service function (storage, a lean-to kitchen) is a later, informally sited shed addition.
service_zone_strategy.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Palladian 'barchesse-wings-and-service-basement' rule -- an estate-management apparatus (subordinate agricultural wings, a rusticated basement) with no relationship to a single-pen frontier house.

street_relationship.rule: There is no street relationship in the urban sense; the house sits informally on its cleared ground, oriented by the site and the slope rather than by a street wall.
street_relationship.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Renaissance palazzo 'blank-rusticated-street-face-courtyard-lit' rule -- an urban Italian palace-front device with no relevance to an isolated frontier clearing.

outbuilding_types.rule: A dispersed cluster of small single-purpose log or frame outbuildings around a yard -- smokehouse, corn crib, springhouse -- consistent with a wall that cannot be lengthened, so a new function gets a new building rather than an enlargement of the old one.
outbuilding_types.note: Retains the substance of the inherited scandinavian-log-vernacular answer (a real and directly relevant parallel -- a wall length limit produces a dispersed farmstead in both traditions) but restated on this node's own ground without that source's specific 'at least eight buildings' figure, which is not independently attested for the American branch.

landscape_idiom.rule: A frontier clearing worked by the household itself -- no designed garden of any kind, terraced or otherwise; the working ground is a cleared field, not a composed landscape.
landscape_idiom.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Mediterranean terraced-retaining-wall-and-axial-approach idiom (italian-villa-vernacular / tuscan-vernacular) with no textual relationship to the American frontier clearing this node's own long description repeatedly evokes.
